verdicts.summary: [L] proves less than [M] prints. [M] prints `vanishes to order at least $j$ at every nonzero alias`.
evidence: [M] prints that the averaging symbol (b_l^j, which is massFilter P p = area P.L p ^ P.J with order_cut : 4 <= J) "vanishes to order at least j at every nonzero alias". [L] states only `vanishing_box : massFilter P.patch (aliasAt 0 l)=0` for l != 0. The fact that area itself vanishes there (hv) appears only inside that proof, and no declaration states an order of vanishing or the vanishing of derivatives below order J. Getting order >= J from the J-th power needs an unwritten Leibniz or analyticity argument, so this claim has no counterpart beyond order one. The finding stands as weaker, and it is not a typo: the proof (B-section.tex:343) argues the order deliberately.

[M] prints that the averaging symbol equals one at zero and 'vanishes to order at least j at every nonzero alias'. [L] has filter_zero (massFilter P.patch 0=1) and vanishing_box (l≠0 → massFilter P.patch (aliasAt 0 l)=0), with massFilter := area P.L p ^ P.J; the nearest quantitative statement, Flight.bills, bounds ‖massFilter (aliasAt p l)‖ ≤ C·decay j l = C·(mix l)^(-j) on a fixed cube, which is decay in the alias index l, not a factor |p|^j as p→0. No declaration states an order of vanishing; deriving it from the J-th power form and analyticity of area is an argument [L] does not write, so the item is weaker in that clause. Not a typo: the remaining clauses are as claimed.
